hook: Docker Desktop is free at 249 employees and paid at 250: 200 developers × $15 = $3,000/month for the same binary. Podman has no seat price at all, which is why the real comparison is not daemon versus daemonless but which company may run the free one.

sections.title: Docker licenses the desktop; Podman has no paid tier
sections.content:
For teams paying for Docker Desktop, or about to. Docker's November 2026 pricing and licence terms distinguish the engine from the desktop:

> **Docker:** the engine is open source; the desktop is a licensed product.
> **Podman:** the runtime has no daemon; the desktop uses Apache License 2.0.

- Docker Engine and Moby stay open source; Docker Desktop uses the Docker Subscription Service Agreement.
- Podman 6.1.4 and Podman Desktop 1.30.5 use Apache License 2.0 with no paid tier.

> Choose paid Docker Desktop for its plan controls; choose Podman when eliminating licence fees justifies Docker-only API rewrites and socket-security responsibility.

sections.title: Commercial Desktop seats become paid at 250 employees or $10 million revenue
sections.content:
Docker Desktop is free while a company has **fewer than 250 employees AND less than $10 million** in annual revenue. Both must hold. Government entities pay at any size.

| Commercial company | Docker Desktop bill |
|---|---|
| 249 employees, under $10M annual revenue | $0 |
| 250 employees or $10M+ annual revenue; 200 users choosing Team | 200 × $15 = $3,000/month; $3,000 × 12 = $36,000/year |

The software did not change between those rows.

| Plan | USD/user/month | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| Personal | $0 | — |
| Pro | $9 | commercial Desktop use, Build Cloud, unlimited private repos |
| Team | $15 | audit logs, role-based access control |
| Business | Contact us for pricing | SSO, SCIM, Hardened Docker Desktop, Image Access Management |

Business publishes no per-seat price. Docker Team's flat $15 per user/month charges for seats, not container usage.

sections.title: Docker's money buys meters, and each meter is its own decision
sections.content:
Past the seat, paid plans attach meters, at Docker's prices:

| Item | Price | Decision it forces |
|---|---|---|
| Build Cloud | base minutes per plan | Do builds fit the allocation? |
| Testcontainers Cloud | $3/100 min prepaid, $4/100 on demand | Steady enough to prepay? |
| Docker Hardened Images | free for developers; production with compliance support starts at $5k/repo | How many repos ship? |
| Docker Offload | licences on Team and Business | Worth the sales call it requires? |

At 4,000 Testcontainers minutes a month: 4,000 ÷ 100 = 40 blocks, so 40 × $4 = $160 on demand or 40 × $3 = $120 prepaid.

- DHI production with compliance support, 12 repos: 12 × $5,000 = $60,000/year floor. Enterprise DHI is quote-only and required for end-of-life software security.
- Build Cloud base minutes reset without accumulating; purchased extras expire each period. Buy extras only for work you expect to consume in that period.

sections.title: Who should not pick Podman: teams without socket ownership
sections.content:
Podman's licence bill is $0. Its `podman system service` provides Docker v1.40 compatibility beside the native Libpod API. Socket-activated by systemd, it exits after 5 idle seconds by default.

With a rootless API service already listening:

```bash
export DOCKER_HOST=unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock
```

Check required API calls and rewrite Docker-only handlers. The command is unavailable directly on macOS or Windows; `--time 0` disables inactivity timeout.

The man page warns:

> "the API grants full access to all Podman functionality, and thus allows arbitrary code execution as the user running the API, with no ability to limit or audit this access"

Rootless narrows whose account is exposed; it does not make the socket safe to share.

- Skip Podman if required API calls are unsupported or nobody owns socket permissions.
- Avoid TCP exposure without mutual TLS; the man page suggests SSH forwarding instead.

sections.title: Who should not pick Docker: government expecting free Desktop
sections.content:
Podman Desktop is free, Apache 2.0 and, in its own words, "trusted as part of the CNCF". It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. Red Hat sells enterprise support as a build, the Red Hat Build of Podman Desktop, not as a licence tier.

- Docker Business includes SOC 2, SSO and SCIM, plus Hardened Docker Desktop and Image Access Management.
- Podman Desktop's enterprise path is that Red Hat build: support and long-term maintenance, not a licence tier.

Skip Docker if you are a government entity counting on the free tier; it never applied.

sections.title: Who should pay Docker, and who should fund the port?
sections.content:
- Choose Docker Business for SSO, SCIM or Image Access Management; choose Team when audit logs and role-based access control meet your governance needs.
- Choose Podman below both free-tier limits if you can fund Docker-only API changes and own socket access before crossing either limit. So should a large org that wants per-seat × headcount off the budget and can staff the port.
- For 25 developers, Podman costs $0 in licence fees plus the port: Docker-only handler rewrites and socket security.

Business gates SSO, SCIM and Image Access Management; every plan carries Build Cloud minutes.

Check today:

1. Headcount and revenue against 250 and $10M. Both limits, not either.
2. Which CI jobs call the Docker API, and at what version.
3. Who can open the socket on your build hosts.

decision_matrix.situation: Commercial company with fewer than 250 employees AND less than $10 million annual revenue; team can fund Docker-only API changes and own socket security before growth
decision_matrix.why: Choose Podman to avoid future Desktop seat fees when the port is funded and socket access has an owner; keeping free Desktop is also available below both limits.

decision_matrix.situation: Commercial company at 249 employees, below $10 million annual revenue, hiring toward 250; a funded Podman port can finish before crossing the boundary
decision_matrix.why: Employee 250 bills every commercial Desktop seat at once, so the port or the budget line has to exist before the hire, not after.

decision_matrix.situation: Commercial company with fewer than 250 employees and annual revenue of $10 million or more requires audit logs and role-based access control
decision_matrix.why: The free tier needs both limits to hold, and the revenue test has already failed. Team adds the required audit logs and role-based access control.

decision_matrix.situation: Government entity of any size with a feasible, staffed Docker-only API port and named socket owner; Business controls are not required
decision_matrix.why: Docker Desktop's free tier never covers government, while Podman has no seat to license.

decision_matrix.situation: The identity team requires SSO, SCIM and Image Access Management
decision_matrix.why: Those are documented Business plan gates; request pricing because the page publishes no per-seat figure.

decision_matrix.situation: Large org wants the seat line deleted; its platform team owns CI sockets and can fund Docker-only API rewrites
decision_matrix.why: Licence fees become $0; the funded rewrites and socket-access responsibility stay with the platform team.

decision_matrix.situation: Committed Testcontainers Cloud usage of 4,000 runtime minutes per month
decision_matrix.why: 4,000 ÷ 100 = 40 blocks; 40 × $3 = $120/month prepaid versus 40 × $4 = $160/month on demand. Choose pre-purchase for this committed usage.

decision_matrix.situation: Mid-term on an annual Docker Team or Business plan with every seat assigned; a funded Podman migration is planned
decision_matrix.pick: Prepare the Podman port before renewal
decision_matrix.why: Only unused seats can be removed and a cancelled plan refunds nothing, so plan the port against the renewal date. Paid access continues through the paid cycle; cancellation cannot pause the plan.

cost_math.label: Commercial company below $10 million annual revenue, moving from 249 to 250 employees; 200 Desktop users choosing Team
cost_math.formula: Previously $0 under both free-tier limits; 200 developers × $15 Team = $3,000/month; $3,000 × 12 = $36,000/year

cost_math.label: 25 developers: Team vs Pro
cost_math.result: $4,500/year vs $2,700/year; Pro drops org audit logs and RBAC

cost_math.label: Docker Hardened Images production with compliance support, 12 repositories
cost_math.result: $60,000/year floor, before Business seats; enterprise DHI is quote-only and required for end-of-life software security

verdict_summary: Pick Podman if your company sits under both free-use limits and you can fund the port, or if you are past them and want per-seat × headcount off the budget. Pick Docker if SSO, SCIM and Image Access Management have to arrive in one contract, or if Build Cloud minutes belong on the same invoice as the desktop.

faqs.q: What happens if a Docker invoice is unpaid?
faqs.a: An unpaid invoice starts a 15-day grace period.

faqs.q: Is Docker Desktop free for our open-source work?
faqs.a: It is free for non-commercial open source, education and personal use. Commercial use beyond the small-business tier needs a Pro, Team or Business subscription, open source or not.

faqs.q: Can CI reach the Podman API over TCP?
faqs.a: The man page recommends against exposing the socket over TCP without mutual TLS and suggests SSH forwarding instead. The service supports only one listening socket, and the rootful default is unix:///run/podman/podman.sock.

faqs.q: Does Podman Desktop work on a locked-down network?
faqs.a: Podman Desktop's vendor lists VPN/proxy support and air-gapped installation options. Check which of those network and installation options matches your environment's restrictions.
